headline: Three-run eighth lifts Brewers past Phillies, 5-1
recap: The Phillies lost to the Milwaukee Brewers 5-1 at Citizens Bank Park on Thursday night, dropping the finale of their three-game series. Sal Frelick's RBI double in the top of the second gave Milwaukee a 1-0 lead, but Philadelphia answered in the bottom of the third when Bryce Harper's RBI single drove in Kyle Schwarber to tie it 1-1. The game stayed even until the eighth, when the Brewers strung together three straight RBI singles — from Jake Bauers, Cooper Pratt and Joey Ortiz — off reliever José Alvarado to take a 4-1 lead, and Jackson Chourio added a solo home run in the ninth to make it 5-1. Andrew Painter started for Philadelphia and allowed just the one run over six innings with eight strikeouts and three walks. Alvarado (5-4) took the loss, JoJo Romero (3-3) got the win for Milwaukee, and Antonio Senzatela closed it out for his fourth save. Harper and Schwarber each had two hits for a Phillies offense held to four hits overall.
The loss dropped Philadelphia to 87-72, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves, and extended the Phillies' losing streak to two games.

Philadelphia opens a three-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday at Citizens Bank Park, with Cristopher Sánchez starting for the Phillies against Rays starter Freddy Peralta. First pitch is scheduled for 6:41 PM ET. The Phillies are favored at -171 on the moneyline, with Tampa Bay at +141.
